```{ojs _filter-checkbox}
//| output: false

// categorical filter input: a checkbox list that keeps every value visible,
// plus group actions and a per-value "only" for isolating a single value.
// wraps Inputs.checkbox, so .value stays an array in data order and the
// element still works as a viewof
filter_checkbox = (values, options = {}) => {
  // actions: false keeps the counter but drops only/all/none, for variables
  // with so few values that isolating one is not worth the extra controls
  const { actions = true, ...rest } = options
  const input = Inputs.checkbox(values, { value: values, ...rest })
  const rows = input.querySelector("div") // the div holding one label per value

  // set the selection and notify downstream cells (the setter alone is silent)
  const set = (vals) => {
    input.value = vals
    input.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true }))
  }

  const action = (text, fun, cls = "cat-action") => {
    const el = html`<button type="button" class=${cls}>${text}</button>`
    el.onclick = (event) => {
      event.preventDefault()
      event.stopPropagation()
      fun()
    }
    return el
  }

  if (actions) {
    // group actions
    rows.before(html`<div class="cat-header">
      ${action("all", () => set(values))}
      ${action("none", () => set([]))}
    </div>`)

    // per-value "only": lives inside the pill, and is always in the layout (just
    // faded) so that revealing it on hover does not reflow the wrapped pills
    const labels = [...rows.children]
    labels.forEach((label, i) => {
      const btn = action("only", () => set([values[i]]), "cat-only")
      btn.title = `only ${values[i]}`
      label.append(btn)
    })
  }

  // selection summary, shown in the callout header so that it is readable while
  // the callout is collapsed. the input is not in the document yet when this
  // cell runs, so wait for it to be inserted before looking for the header
  let header_count = null
  requestAnimationFrame(() => {
    const header = input.closest(".callout")?.querySelector(".callout-title-container")
    if (!header) return
    // the cell re-runs whenever the values change (e.g. switching data source),
    // and the header lives outside the cell output, so a summary left behind by
    // a previous instance has to be cleared rather than appended to
    header.querySelectorAll(".cat-summary").forEach(el => el.remove())
    header_count = html`<span class="cat-summary"></span>`
    header.append(header_count)
    update()
  })

  const update = () => {
    if (header_count) header_count.textContent = `${input.value.length} of ${values.length}`
  }
  input.addEventListener("input", update)
  update()

  return input
}
```

```{ojs _filter-checkbox-styles}
//| output: false
html`<style>
  .cat-header {
    display: flex;
    align-items: baseline;
    gap: 0.3em;
    margin-bottom: 0.35em;
    /* the inputs form is a wrapping flex container, so claim the whole line to
       keep short checkbox sets from sitting next to the buttons */
    flex: 0 0 100%;
  }

  /* button-like, but outlined rather than filled so they read as actions
     rather than as another value pill.
     quarto tags buttons in cell output with .btn-quarto, and layout.scss styles
     those via div.cell-output-display, so these selectors have to be specific
     enough to win against it (and against .oi-* button { font: inherit }) */
  .cat-header button.cat-action {
    background: none;
    border: 1px solid #ccc;
    border-radius: 0.5rem;
    padding: 0.1rem 0.5rem;
    font-size: 0.7rem;
    color: #333;
    cursor: pointer;
  }

  .cat-header button.cat-action:hover {
    background-color: #fbe4b4;
    border-color: #999;
  }

  .cat-summary {
    margin-left: 0.5em;
    font-weight: normal;
    font-style: italic;
    opacity: 0.7;
  }

  /* the pill is the <label>; keep the only-button in flow but faded.
     quarto gives these buttons bootstrap's .btn classes, so .btn:hover paints a
     background behind them -- turning that off needs a selector that
     out-specifies it, and the hover cue is the text colour instead */
  label button.cat-only {
    border: none;
    background: none;
    padding: 0 0 0 0.35em;
    margin: 0;
    font-size: 0.75em;
    line-height: 1;
    color: #333;
    cursor: pointer;
    opacity: 0.3;
  }

  /* revealed by hovering anywhere on the pill */
  label:hover button.cat-only {
    opacity: 1;
  }

  /* highlighted by hovering the word itself. !important because bootstrap's
     .btn:hover paints a background and colour here, and out-specifying it is
     brittle -- quarto adds the .btn classes to these buttons behind our back */
  label button.cat-only:hover,
  label button.cat-only:focus {
    background: none !important;
    box-shadow: none !important;
    color: #2c728e !important;
    opacity: 1;
  }
</style>`
```
